tecnicas.nome_original: agentic pipeline (multi-agent, feedback-driven architecture; agentic compilation repair pipeline)
tecnicas.localizador: PDF p. 2, Fig. 1; PDF p. 6, seção V-D e Fig. 6; PDF p. 7, Fig. 7
tecnicas.observacao: Pacote com três agentes (Questioner, Compilation e Execution) que encadeia tradução, compilação e execução, com reparos guiados por mensagens do compilador (Clang++, NVCC) e erros de execução, até 3 tentativas por agente. Comparado com a condição Without agent (só a tradução inicial do Questioner). É pacote híbrido: os agentes de Compilation e Execution usam sempre GPT-4o-mini, de modo que, quando o Questioner é LLaMA-3.3-70B-Instruct, a condição com agente também introduz outro modelo (componente fora do escopo, selecao_modelo); o ganho é do pacote e não pode ser atribuído a um mecanismo isolado (feedback, multiagente ou decomposição).

tecnicas.localizador: PDF p. 6, seção V-D; PDF p. 7, Fig. 8 e «Ablation Study: Effectiveness of Compilation Agent in repairing errors»
tecnicas.observacao: Compila o código e, em caso de falha, formula prompt de reparo com a mensagem de erro. A Fig. 8 mostra só a contribuição cumulativa por tentativa de reparo (tradução inicial, tentativa 1, tentativa 2), sem condição com o Execution Agent e sem o Compilation Agent; não há isolamento do componente dentro do pacote.
Executa o código compilado e, se a verificação de saída falha, produz prompt de reparo com o comportamento observado (erros de execução), até 3 tentativas. Não há condição que retire só este agente.

riscos.descricao: Modelos sem adaptação têm baixa compilação e correção funcional nas configurações padrão (GPT-4o-mini: 46% de compilação e 15% de correção funcional, segundo o resumo).

No few-shot, mesmo com amostras semelhantes ou idênticas ao exemplo do prompt, o LLaMA introduz erros sintáticos sutis e críticos; os autores suspeitam de diluição de contexto com prompts mais longos e do caráter do few-shot; com 3-shot o desempenho cai visivelmente.

citacoes.trecho: Specifically, in this work, we target translations between serial code, CUDA, and OpenMP.

Our findings reveal that while off-the-shelf models struggle under the default settings (e.g., GPT-4o-mini achieves only 46% compilation and 15% functional correctness), our UniPar methodology – combining fine-tuning, hyperparameter tuning, and compiler-guided repair – improves performance by up to 2X (69% compilation and 33% correctness).
To assess its effect in our setting, we compared the compilation rates of generated code with 0-shot, 1-shot, 2-shot, and 3-shot configurations.
Each n-shot involved appending n additional examples for the same source–target language pair from the PARATRANS train set.
System: You are an HPC expert specializing in translating between parallel programming APIs.

While the exact cause of the poor LLM performance with the few-shot prompting would warrant further investigation, specific examples reveal that even on samples similar or identical to the one-shot prompt, LLaMA-3.3-70B-Instruct still introduces subtle but critical syntactic errors.

We suspect this results from a combination of context dilution with longer prompts and the nature of few-shot prompting, which is most effective at guiding answers’ high-level structure and less at capturing fine-grained details within that structure.
Prior studies have shown that LLM performance may degrade when processing long or unbalanced inputs, as the context window becomes saturated or loses focus [45].
We set a cut-off of 7,500 tokens, determined empirically by analyzing the token distribution of source files using the LLaMA-3.3-70B-Instruct tokenizer.

This suggests that reduced randomness in the token selection process improves syntactic validity, especially when generating larger kernel codes, as supported by the findings in previous work [56], [57].
Questioner Agent: Assembles the initial prompts that define the source and target languages (e.g., CUDA → OpenMP).
Compilation Agent: Attempts to compile the generated code. If the compilation fails, it extracts the error message and formulates a compilation repair prompt for its model.
Execution Agent: Executes the code that passes compilation. If output verification fails, it produces an output-repair prompt containing the observed behavior and invokes its model for a correction.
Both the Compilation and Execution agents used 3 rounds with GPT-4o-mini as their underlying LLM.
In general, incorporating compiler and output verifier feedback significantly improves overall performance in terms of compilation and validation rate.

This stems from the behavior of the model used by the compilation agent that manages to solve only one of two types of issues in each iteration, so codes with multiple needed corrections require more than one iteration.
citacoes.localizador: PDF p. 7, ablação do Compilation Agent

citacoes.trecho: To support a fair evaluation, we split the dataset into a training set and a held-out test set, as shown in Table I.

Although we checked the syntax and the functional correctness of the translated code, we did not check its runtime performance or scalability – factors that are typically important for an HPC application – nor did we ask LLMs to optimize them.
